meta.titulo: Porsche IMS bearing: diagnosis and repair · Valentín Motors
meta.descripcion: Preventive replacement of the Porsche IMS bearing in M96 and M97 engines, including preliminary diagnosis and published pricing by model.

secciones.titulo: Preventive replacement at a fixed price
parrafos: We replace the intermediate shaft bearing on M96 and M97 engines at a fixed price for models from 1997 to 2006, with both manual and automatic transmissions. We have performed this procedure dozens of times, covering all three bearing revisions installed by Porsche.

Preventive replacement does not require opening the engine block: the transmission and the flywheel or flexplate are removed, and the bearing is accessed via the flange. The engine is not disassembled, keeping the cost reasonable compared to the expense of a failure.

secciones.titulo: Identifying the bearing before starting work
parrafos: The IMS procedure begins by identifying the specific bearing for the model, year, and—in transition years—the engine number.
items: Inspection of the installed bearing upon access.

imagenes.alt: M96 3.4 engine block on the stand, with the bores exposed

parrafos: The published preventive service targets M96 and M97 engines, as well as models where the bearing can be replaced without opening the engine block.

Not all IMS units carry the same risk or allow for the same type of intervention. If metal particles or noise are already present, the preventive approach is halted, and the damage is assessed before restarting the engine.

imagenes.alt: Complete M96 teardown sorted into trays: camshafts, cylinder head and hardware

parrafos: The failure affects the 911 (996 and 997.1 generations), the Boxster (986 and 987), and the Cayman, spanning the years 1997 to 2008. Not all models use the same bearing, and that is the key difference: the single-row 6204 bearing installed between 2000 and 2005 has shown the highest failure rate, yet it is also the easiest to replace.

If the car you are interested in falls into that group and there is no record of any work having been done on it, preventive replacement is the low-cost option. If the engine is already making noise or metal particles appear in the oil, the window for preventive action has passed; instead, an assessment is required before starting the engine again.

secciones.titulo: How to tell if your car is affected
parrafos: We have published a calculator that provides answers based on the model and year: it indicates which bearing your specific unit is fitted with, whether it can be replaced without opening the engine, and what checks are required. For the transition years—2000, 2001, and 2005—it also asks for the engine number, as two different bearings were used during those periods and the year alone is not enough to distinguish between them.
The calculator does not diagnose the car's current condition. It states what was installed at the factory; the only way to know what is inside now is to open it up.

items: Preliminary diagnosis: analysis of the oil and filter, checking for particles.
Removal of the transmission, flywheel or flexplate, and the IMS flange.
Replacement of the bearing with the kit appropriate for the specific service level.
Replacement of the intermediate shaft seal and the clutch, if applicable.
Reassembly, final adjustments, and road test.
Mechanical warranty on the work performed.

secciones.titulo: Is the year enough to know which IMS it has?
parrafos: Not always. Different revisions can coexist in the 2000, 2001, and 2005 model years, so the engine number helps identify the configuration.

secciones.titulo: Does replacing the IMS require opening the engine?
parrafos: For units eligible for the preventive procedure, access is gained by removing the gearbox and the flywheel or flexplate. If internal damage already exists, the approach changes.
